title: Commutes Mark Shapiro’s 85-Year Prison Sentence to Time Served
description_medium: On December 23, 2020, President Donald Trump commuted Mark Shapiro’s 85-year prison sentence to time served and directed his immediate release. Shapiro had been convicted of conspiracy and securities, wire and mail fraud. The grant left more than $22 million in restitution and three years of supervised release in place.
description_long: On December 23, 2020, President Donald Trump commuted Mark Shapiro’s prison sentence to time served and directed the Bureau of Prisons to release him immediately. Shapiro had received an 85-year sentence after a jury convicted him of conspiracy and offenses involving securities, wire and mail fraud. The DOJ warrant states that he had been confined since the jury’s November 2009 verdict and faced a projected release date in 2078. The commutation left a $22,075,631 restitution obligation, a $500 assessment and three years of supervised release in effect. Trump’s warrant said the ends of justice did not require continued confinement until the projected release date and that community safety would not be compromised. Shapiro had faced a projected release date of August 31, 2078, after serving continuously since the jury returned its verdict. The clemency warrant documents that this change affected imprisonment only: restitution, the special assessment and supervised release continued under the original judgment.
rationale: The signed warrant specifies the commuted sentence, immediate release, continuing obligations and stated grounds.
